decisions.choice: to Moses and to Aaron: both brothers receive the order for the camp
decisions.reason: Aaron shared in the count of chapter 1 (1:3, 17, 44), and the arrangement that follows builds on that count, tribe by tribe. Aaron as high priest also had charge of the sanctuary that stands at the center of the camp (verse 17; 3:38).

decisions.choice: He said,
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "saying" introduces the words that follow. Balanced makes it a short sentence of its own, as in other chapters; Readable folds it into "said to".

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "il dit"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit"); the LORD's instructions in the future at Literal and Balanced ("camperont", "partiront"), "doivent" or the future at Readable
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1 and the French style guide: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken French, which Readable uses. The order for the camp (verses 2-31) is an instruction for the future, so it is in the future tense.

records.literal_gloss: Each by his standard, with [the] signs of [the] house of their fathers, will camp [the] sons of Israel; from opposite, around the tent of meeting, they will camp.

en.L: "Each by his standard, with the signs of the house of their fathers, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall camp; at a distance all around the tent of meeting they shall camp.
en.B: "The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to camp with each group under its own standard, beside the emblems of their ancestral families. They are to camp all around the tent of meeting, at a distance from it.
en.R: "The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must set up camp all around the meeting tent, some distance away from it. Each group will camp under its own flag, with the signs of its families.

ko.L: "이스라엘 자손은 각자 자기 깃발 곁에, 자기 조상의 집의 표지들과 함께 진을 칠 것이다. 회막 둘레로 마주 보며 떨어져서 진을 칠 것이다.
ko.B: "이스라엘 백성은 각 무리가 자기 깃발 아래, 자기 집안의 표지 곁에 진을 쳐야 한다. 회막에서 조금 떨어져서 그 둘레에 진을 쳐야 한다.
ko.R: "이스라엘 사람들은 회막에서 조금 떨어진 곳에 회막을 빙 둘러 진을 쳐야 한다. 각 무리는 자기 깃발 아래, 자기 집안을 나타내는 표시와 함께 진을 쳐야 한다.

decisions.choice: standard ... signs: a large flag for each camp, and smaller marks for each family
alternatives: each tribe had its own standard
decisions.reason: The first word names a standard or banner raised on a pole, the rallying point of a large body of people. Verse 3 and the verses after it speak of "the standard of the camp of Judah", so each standard seems to belong to a camp of three tribes. The second word means "signs" or "marks", here the emblems that showed each ancestral family its place. The text does not describe what any standard or sign looked like.

decisions.choice: from opposite, all around: facing the tent on every side, but at a distance
decisions.reason: The phrase means "over against" or "at a distance facing". The tribes face the tent of meeting from all four sides but keep a space between themselves and it. The Levites camp in that space, so that no anger falls on the people for coming too near (1:52-53; 3:23-38).

decisions.choice: each: every tribe, or every camp, in its place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "man", used as "each". It refers to the units of the people, each in its place under its standard, and not to men alone: the whole people camp this way, families and all.

decisions.choice: each group
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "each". Balanced and Readable say "each group" so that the sentence does not seem to give every person a flag; verses 3-31 show that the groups are tribes gathered into four camps.

decisions.choice: flag
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word "flag" for the standard; Literal and Balanced keep "standard" through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "les signes" (L, R); "les emblèmes" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means signs or marks, here the marks that showed each ancestral family its place (m1). Literal and Readable keep the plain "signes"; Balanced says "emblèmes", the usual French word for a mark that stands for a group, as the English says "emblems". "Enseignes" was avoided because it would be taken for a second kind of flag.

decisions.choice: "bendera" for the standard; "alama" for the signs
decisions.reason: Swahili has one everyday word, "bendera", for both a standard and a flag, so it stands at every level where the English has "standard" (L, B) and "flag" (R). The family signs are "alama", marks, which keeps them distinct from the large standard of each camp (m1).

decisions.choice: "dấu hiệu" (L, R) / "huy hiệu" (B) for the signs of the families
decisions.reason: These are smaller marks for each family beside the tribe's banner; "huy hiệu" names an emblem in standard Vietnamese, and Literal and Readable keep the plain "dấu hiệu".

decisions.choice: "깃발" for the standard of each camp and "표지" (Literal, Balanced) / "표시" (Readable) for the signs of each family
decisions.reason: The meaning decision distinguishes a large flag for each camp from smaller marks for each family; Korean keeps two different words so the reader sees the two levels. "깃발" is the word already used in 1:52.

decisions.choice: "마주 보며 떨어져서" for "from opposite"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the tribes face the tent from a distance; the Literal keeps both ideas, the other levels keep only the distance, as the English does.

source.text: וְהַחֹנִים֙ קֵ֣דְמָה מִזְרָ֔חָה דֶּ֛גֶל מַחֲנֵ֥ה יְהוּדָ֖ה לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְנָשִׂיא֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה נַחְשׁ֖וֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And those camping eastward, toward [the] sunrise, [the] standard of [the] camp of Judah by their armies; and [the] leader of [the] sons of Judah [is] Nahshon son of Amminadab.

en.L: And those camping on the east side, toward the sunrise, [shall be] the standard of the camp of Judah by their armies, and the leader of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah [shall be] Nahshon son of Amminadab.
en.B: Those who camp on the east side, toward the sunrise, are to be the camp of Judah under its standard, by their divisions. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
en.R: The camp of Judah, with its troops, will be on the east side, where the sun rises. It will camp under Judah's flag. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.

ko.L: 그리고 동쪽, 곧 해 돋는 쪽으로 진을 칠 자들은 그들의 군대별로 유다 진의 깃발[에 속한 자들]이요, 유다 자손의 지도자는 아미나답의 아들 나손[이다].
ko.B: 동쪽, 곧 해 돋는 쪽에는 유다 진이 부대별로 자기 깃발 아래 진을 쳐야 한다. 유다 자손의 지도자는 아미나답의 아들 나손이다.
ko.R: 유다 진은 부대별로 해가 뜨는 동쪽에 진을 칠 것이다. 그들은 유다의 깃발 아래 진을 친다. 유다 사람들의 지도자는 아미나답의 아들 나손이다.

decisions.choice: east, toward the sunrise: the front of the camp
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two words for east, "to the front" and "to the sunrise". The entrance of the tabernacle faced east (Exodus 27:13-16), and Moses, Aaron and his sons camped on that side, in front of it (3:38). Judah takes the east, the side of the entrance, and leads the march (verse 9).

decisions.choice: their armies: the companies of fighting men
decisions.reason: The word names an army or a body of men in military service. The men counted in chapter 1 were those "able to go out to war" (1:3), and here they are grouped into the units in which they camp and march.

decisions.choice: an order for the future, with no verb
decisions.reason: The sentence has no verb; the Hebrew simply sets the parts side by side: "those camping on the east, the standard of the camp of Judah". It is part of the LORD's instruction, so it describes how the camp is to be arranged.

decisions.choice: Nahshon son of Amminadab: the same leader named in 1:7
decisions.reason: Nahshon was the brother of Aaron's wife Elisheba (Exodus 6:23), and he appears among the ancestors of David (Ruth 4:20; 1 Chronicles 2:10-11).

decisions.choice: armies / divisions / troops
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "armies" for the word through the chapter. Balanced says "divisions", since one tribe's force is a part of the whole army of Israel, and Readable says "troops" or "army".

decisions.choice: The camp of Judah ... will be on the east side ... It will camp under Judah's flag.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the camp first and gives the flag a sentence of its own, so that the point (where Judah camps) comes first.

decisions.choice: "al oriente, hacia la salida del sol" (L); "del lado oriental" (B); "en el lado este" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives two words for east (m1). Literal and Balanced use "oriente", the word Spanish has long used for the side of the sunrise, and keep "hacia la salida del sol"; Readable says the everyday "este" and explains "por donde sale el sol".

decisions.choice: "le chef du peuple de Juda" (and so for each tribe)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the sons of Judah", meaning the tribe as a whole. Balanced and Readable say "le peuple de Juda", as the English says "the people of Judah", which takes in the whole tribe without the gender setting; Literal keeps "les enfants (fils) de Juda" with the setting, as for the sons of Israel.

decisions.choice: "upande wa mashariki, kuelekea mawio ya jua" (L, B); "jua linapochomoza" (R)
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words for east (m1) become "mashariki" and "mawio ya jua", the place of the sunrise. Readable says it with the everyday verb, "where the sun rises".

decisions.choice: "군대" (Literal) and "부대" (Balanced, Readable) for "armies"; "유다 자손" (Literal, Balanced) / "유다 사람들" (Readable) for "the sons of Judah"
decisions.reason: As in 1:3: the companies of fighting men of each tribe. The tribe's people follow the pattern of "이스라엘 자손 / 백성 / 사람들".

decisions.choice: "đạo quân" (L) / "đội quân" (B, R) for the tribes' armies
decisions.reason: The word names the companies of fighting men in each tribe; "đạo quân" keeps the older military word at Literal, and "đội quân" is the everyday word for a body of troops. Used through chapter 2.

decisions.choice: "Người lãnh đạo của họ" for "the leader of the people of Judah" at Readable
decisions.reason: The tribe has just been named, so Readable avoids saying it a second time in the same short paragraph; the person meant is the same.

en.R: His army has 74,600 men.

es.R: Sus tropas suman 74 600 hombres.

fr.L: Et son armée, et leurs recensés, [sont] 74 600.
fr.B: Sa division compte 74 600 hommes.
fr.R: Ses troupes comptent 74 600 hommes.

sw.L: Na jeshi lake, na walioandikishwa wao, [ni] 74,600.
sw.B: Kikosi chake kina wanaume 74,600.
sw.R: Vikosi vyake vina wanaume 74,600.

vi.R: Đội quân của ông có 74.600 người.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 군대, 곧 그들의 계수된 자는 74,600[명이다].
ko.B: 그의 부대는 74,600명이다.
ko.R: 그의 군대는 74,600명이다.

decisions.choice: his army ... their enrolled: the force of Judah under its leader
decisions.reason: "His" may point to Nahshon, the leader just named, or to Judah as a tribe; "their" points to the people of the tribe. Either way the sentence gives the size of Judah's force. The same formula follows each tribe in the chapter, sometimes with "his counted" in place of "their counted" (verses 6, 8, 11), with no change of sense.

decisions.choice: 74,600: the number counted for Judah in 1:27
decisions.reason: Each figure in this chapter repeats the count of chapter 1. On the word "thousand" and the size of these numbers, see the note at the census in chapter 1: the word can also name a clan or military unit, which would give much smaller totals.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their enrolled". Balanced and Readable add "men", since those counted were males twenty years old and up who could serve in the army (1:3). Literal brackets the word.

decisions.choice: "sus tropas" at Readable (and so in verses 6-30)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "tropas", the word chosen for this Hebrew word in chapter 1, where the English Readable says "army" in this formula; each tribe's men are a part of the one army of Israel.

decisions.choice: "ses troupes" at Readable (and so in verses 6-30)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word chosen for this Hebrew word in chapter 1, "troupes", where the English Readable says "army" in this formula; "son armée" would make each tribe a separate army, while the men of all the tribes form the one army of Israel.

decisions.choice: "vikosi vyake" at Readable (and so in verses 6-30)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "vikosi", the word used for this Hebrew word at Balanced and Readable since chapter 1; "jeshi lake" would make each tribe a separate army.

decisions.choice: "ông" for the tribal leader ("his army")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "his" points back to the leader just named, and "ông" is the respectful pronoun for him in plain modern Vietnamese.

source.text: וְהַחֹנִ֥ים עָלָ֖יו מַטֵּ֣ה יִשָּׂשכָ֑ר וְנָשִׂיא֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשָּׂשכָ֔ר נְתַנְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־צוּעָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And those camping next to him [the] tribe of Issachar; and [the] leader of [the] sons of Issachar [is] Nethanel son of Zuar.

en.L: And those camping next to him [shall be] the tribe of Issachar, and the leader of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Issachar [shall be] Nethanel son of Zuar.
en.B: Next to Judah the tribe of Issachar is to camp. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.

ko.B: 유다 진에 계수된 사람은 부대별로 모두 186,400명이다. 그들이 맨 먼저 출발해야 한다.

decisions.choice: set out: pull up the tent pegs and move on
decisions.reason: The verb first meant pulling up the pegs of a tent, and so breaking camp and setting out on a journey. Chapter 10 tells how the camps set out in this order when the cloud lifted (10:11-28).

decisions.choice: first: Judah leads the march
decisions.reason: The camp on the east, in front of the entrance of the tabernacle, goes at the head of the line (10:14). Judah's place at the front fits the blessing of Judah in Genesis 49:8-10.

decisions.choice: the total of the three tribes
decisions.reason: The figure is the sum of verses 4, 6 and 8: 74,600 + 54,400 + 57,400 = 186,400.

decisions.choice: march out
decisions.reason: Readable says "march out", since the people move as an army in ranks; Literal and Balanced say "set out".

decisions.choice: "nhổ trại ra đi" (B), "lên đường" (R) for "set out"
decisions.reason: The verb pictures pulling up tent pegs to move on; "nhổ trại" says just that in Vietnamese. Literal keeps the plain "ra đi". Used for the march order in chapters 2 and 4.

decisions.choice: "출발하다" for "set out" (Literal, Balanced); "행진해 나가다" at Readable
decisions.reason: The verb pictures pulling up the tent pegs to move on; "출발하다" is the plain word for a company setting off, and the Readable follows the English "march out".

decisions.choice: south: the right-hand side
decisions.reason: The word for south comes from the word for the right hand. Facing east, toward the sunrise, the south lies on the right.

decisions.choice: Reuben, Simeon and Gad: the second camp
decisions.reason: Reuben was Jacob's firstborn (Genesis 29:32), but his camp comes second, after Judah's (verse 16; compare Genesis 49:3-4, 8). Simeon was Leah's second son, and Gad the son of Zilpah, Leah's servant (Genesis 30:9-11).

decisions.choice: Elizur son of Shedeur: the leader named in 1:5
decisions.reason: The leaders in this chapter are the twelve men who helped Moses and Aaron with the count (1:4-16), named in the same order of camps in 7:12-83 and 10:14-27.

decisions.choice: Reuel: the same man as Deuel in 1:14
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text here reads Reuel, but the father of Eliasaph is Deuel in 1:14; 7:42, 47 and 10:20. The two Hebrew letters for d and r look very much alike and were easily confused in copying. Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Latin Vulgate read Deuel here, while the Greek translation reads Reuel in all these places. The text followed here reads Reuel; reviewers should check the evidence.

ko.L: 그리고 회막, 곧 레위인의 진이 진들의 한가운데에서 출발할 것이다. 그들이 진을 치는 대로 그렇게 출발하되, 각자 자기 자리에서 그들의 깃발별로 [출발할 것이다].
ko.B: 그다음에 회막이 레위인의 진과 함께 모든 진의 한가운데에서 출발해야 한다. 그들은 진을 친 순서대로, 저마다 자기 자리를 지키며 자기 깃발 아래 출발해야 한다.
ko.R: 그다음에는 회막이 레위인의 진과 함께 모든 진의 한가운데에서 행진해 나갈 것이다. 지파들은 진을 친 순서 그대로 행진할 것이다. 저마다 자기 깃발 아래 자기 자리를 지켜야 한다.

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting, the camp of the Levites: the tent travels with the Levites in the center
decisions.reason: The two phrases stand side by side: the tent of meeting sets out as, or together with, the camp of the Levites, who carry it and camp around it (1:50-53). As the tent stands in the center of the camp at rest, so it moves in the center on the march, between the two camps in front and the two behind. Chapter 10 gives the details: the parts of the tabernacle go after Judah's camp, and the holy things after Reuben's (10:17, 21).

decisions.choice: each on his hand: each in his own place
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means a place or position, as in Numbers 1:52 and Deuteronomy 23:13. Each unit keeps the same position on the march as it has in the camp.

decisions.choice: in the middle: God's dwelling at the center of his people
decisions.reason: The tent where the LORD meets with Israel (Exodus 25:8; 29:42-45) is the center of the whole arrangement. The tribes are placed around it, and the Levites between it and them.

decisions.choice: The tribes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they". Readable names the tribes, the units that keep their places.

decisions.choice: "chacun à sa place"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each on his hand" means each in his own place (m2). A word-for-word "sur sa main" would mean nothing in French, so Literal says "à sa place", as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "자기 자리에서" for "on his hand"
decisions.reason: "On his hand" is a Hebrew idiom for one's own place, as the meaning decision says; a word-for-word "손" would mean nothing in Korean, so the Literal gives the sense.

decisions.choice: seaward: to the west
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "toward the sea", meaning the Mediterranean, which lies west of the land of Canaan. The word was used for "west" even where the sea could not be seen, as here in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin: the descendants of Rachel
decisions.reason: Ephraim and Manasseh were the sons of Joseph, whom Jacob took as his own (Genesis 48:5), and Benjamin was Joseph's full brother; all three tribes descend from Rachel. Ephraim, the younger son, leads, as Jacob said he would be greater (Genesis 48:19-20). The west is the side of the tabernacle opposite the entrance.

records.literal_gloss: But the Levites not were counted in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel, just as commanded Yahweh Moses.

en.L: But the Levites were not enrolled among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses.
en.B: The Levites, however, were not counted among the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.R: But the Levites were not counted with the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

es.L: Pero los levitas no fueron alistados en medio de los hijos de Israel, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mandó a Moisés.
es.B: Los levitas, sin embargo, no fueron alistados con los demás israelitas, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés.
es.R: Pero a los levitas no se les contó con los demás israelitas. Así se lo había mandado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés.

fr.L: Mais les Lévites ne furent pas recensés au milieu des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné à Moïse.
fr.B: Les Lévites, en revanche, ne furent pas recensés avec les autres {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné à Moïse.
fr.R: Mais les Lévites n’ont pas été comptés avec les autres {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. C’est ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Moïse.

sw.L: Lakini Walawi hawakuandikishwa katikati ya wana wa Israeli, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru Musa.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, Walawi hawakuandikishwa pamoja na Waisraeli wengine, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwamuru Musa.
sw.R: Lakini Walawi hawakuhesabiwa pamoja na Waisraeli wengine. Ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwamuru Musa.

vi.L: Nhưng người Lê-vi không được kiểm kê giữa con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se.
vi.B: Tuy nhiên, người Lê-vi không được kiểm kê chung với những người Y-sơ-ra-ên khác, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se.
vi.R: Nhưng người Lê-vi không được đếm chung với những người Y-sơ-ra-ên khác. Đó là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se.

ko.L: 그러나 레위인은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 대로 이스라엘 자손 가운데서 계수되지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 레위인은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 대로 다른 이스라엘 백성과 함께 계수되지 않았다.
ko.R: 그러나 레위인은 다른 이스라엘 사람들과 함께 세지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 그렇게 명령하셨기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the Levites not counted: the command of 1:47-49
decisions.reason: The LORD had told Moses not to count the tribe of Levi with the other tribes, because the Levites were set apart to care for the tabernacle (1:47-53). They are counted on their own in chapter 3, from one month old up (3:14-39).

decisions.choice: the other
decisions.reason: The Levites were themselves sons of Israel; Balanced and Readable add "other" so the sentence does not seem to place them outside Israel.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כֵּֽן־חָנ֤וּ לְדִגְלֵיהֶם֙ וְכֵ֣ן נָסָ֔עוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖יו עַל־בֵּ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel according to all that commanded Yahweh Moses; so they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each by his clans, by [the] house of his fathers.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses; so they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each by his clans, by the house of his fathers.
en.B: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. That is how they camped under their standards, and that is how they set out, each by clan and by ancestral family.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. They camped under their flags and marched out the same way, each with their own clan and family.

es.L: E hicieron los hijos de Israel conforme a todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mandó a Moisés; así acamparon según sus estandartes, y así partieron, cada uno según sus clanes, según la casa de sus padres.
es.B: Así hicieron los israelitas todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés. Así acamparon bajo sus estandartes y así partieron, cada uno con su clan y su familia.
es.R: Los israelitas hicieron todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado a Moisés. Acamparon bajo sus banderas y se pusieron en marcha de la misma manera, cada uno con su clan y su familia.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent selon tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Moïse ; ainsi ils campèrent selon leurs bannières, et ainsi ils partirent, chacun selon ses clans, selon la maison de ses pères.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent donc tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Moïse. C’est ainsi qu’ils campèrent sous leurs bannières et ainsi qu’ils partirent, chacun dans son clan et dans sa famille.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Moïse. Ils ont campé sous leurs drapeaux et se sont mis en marche de la même manière, chacun avec son clan et sa famille.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya sawasawa na yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwamuru Musa; ndivyo walivyopiga kambi kwa bendera zao, na ndivyo walivyosafiri, kila mtu kwa koo zake, kwa nyumba ya baba zake.
sw.B: Basi Waisraeli walifanya kila kitu ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru Musa. Ndivyo walivyopiga kambi chini ya bendera zao, na ndivyo walivyosafiri, kila mmoja pamoja na ukoo wake na jamaa yake.
sw.R: Waisraeli walifanya kila kitu ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru Musa. Walipiga kambi chini ya bendera zao na kusafiri kwa namna ileile, kila mmoja pamoja na ukoo na jamaa yake.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm theo mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se; họ đóng trại theo cờ hiệu mình như vậy, và họ ra đi như vậy, mỗi người theo gia tộc mình, theo nhà cha mình.
vi.B: Vậy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se. Họ đóng trại dưới cờ hiệu mình đúng như vậy, và ra đi cũng đúng như vậy, mỗi người theo gia tộc và gia đình tổ tiên mình.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se. Họ đóng trại dưới lá cờ của mình và lên đường cũng theo cách ấy, mỗi người đi cùng gia tộc và gia đình mình.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 모든 것대로 행하였다. 그렇게 그들은 그들의 깃발별로 진을 쳤고, 그렇게 각자 자기 가문대로, 자기 조상의 집대로 출발하였다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 것을 모두 행하였다. 그들은 그렇게 자기 깃발 아래 진을 쳤고, 그렇게 저마다 가문과 집안별로 출발하였다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 것을 모두 그대로 했다. 그들은 자기 깃발 아래 진을 쳤고, 행진할 때도 저마다 자기 가문과 집안과 함께 그렇게 나아갔다.

decisions.choice: so ... and so: they did exactly as commanded
decisions.reason: "So they camped ... and so they set out" repeats the words of the order in verse 17 ("just as they camp, so they will set out") to show that it was carried out in full. The chapter ends as chapter 1 does, with the people doing all that the LORD commanded (1:54).

decisions.choice: clans and the house of his fathers: the units within each tribe
decisions.reason: A tribe was made up of clans, and a clan of ancestral families (verse 32). The people kept these family groups together in camp and on the march.

decisions.choice: each: every member of the people
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the word "man" means "each". The whole people, not only the men counted, camp and travel by families.

decisions.choice: each by clan / each with their own clan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each by his clans" refers to every member of the people. Balanced avoids the pronoun, and Readable uses "their", so that the sentence does not seem to speak only of men.
